1 1.
The present suit is filed for the recovery of amount of Rs. 1,20,000/- along with interest.

AVERMENTS OF THE PLAINT:
2. Succinctly, the case of plaintiff is that father-in-law and defendant no. 2 are the brother-in-law of plaintiff.

That in the second week of August, 2015, defendant no. 1 approached the plaintiff and asked for loan of Rs. 1,50,000/- as he had to make payments of salary and some dues of the business of defendant no. 2 which was closing down due to heavy losses.

Plaintiff reminded defendant no. 1 that he had already took Rs. 20,000/- in the month of December, 2014 as loan from the plaintiff through cheque which was not returned till now, to which defendant no. 1 promised to also return the said amount of Rs. 20,000/- along with loan amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- before March, 2016.

Keeping in view the urgency of defendants and believing the promise of defendant no. 1, plaintiff gave a cheque of Rs. 1,00,000/- to defendant which was debited from the account of plaintiff on 13.08.2015.
It is averred that in the year 2016, defendant no. 1 started false and frivolous criminal litigation against the plaintiff and did not even return the loan amount.

Consequently, a legal notice dated 19.07.2017 was issued Page no. 2 of 14 (Kanika Agarwal) CJ01/(South) Saket Court/New Delhi MOHAN KUMAR SANGWAN Vs. UPENDRA SINGH AND ANR.
upon defendant no. 1.

sentences.text: In reply dated 31.07.2017, defendant no. 1 admits that he had received two cheques from the plaintiff but falsely alleged that defendant no. 1 gave a loan of Rs. 2,00,000/- on 02.01.2013 to the plaintiff.
Constrained by false allegations of the defendants, the present suit has been filed by the plaintiff.

AVERMENTS OF THE WRITTEN STATEMENT:
3. Per contra, the case of the defendants is that the suit of plaintiff is not maintainable as he has not come before this court with clean hands and suppressed the real and material facts.
It is stated that present suit has been filed only to harass the defendants and to grab money.
It is further stated that there is no cause of action against the defendants.

It is stated that for the marriage of plaintiff's niece Ms. Alka @ Choti on 16.01.2013, the defendants had given Rs. 2,00,000/- as a loan in front of Ms.
Shikha and Mr. Ankit at the residence of the defendants to the plaintiff.

It is stated that plaintiff issued two cheques in favour of defendants and Mr. Nitin Malik/ defendant no. 2 amounting to Rs.
1,00,000/- and Rs. 20,000/- respectively and remaining Rs. 80,000/- is still due towards the plaintiff.
It is stated that due to strained relation with the daughter of the defendant no. 1, plaintiff filed the false and frivolous suit.
All the other averments made by the plaintiff in his plaint are denied by the defendants.
It is prayed that the present suit be dismissed.

During cross-examination, it has been admitted by defendant no. 1 that the documents filed by him relate to the period after the amount of Rs. 1.20 lacs was received by him from the plaintiff.
It is denied that he did not institute any case because he never gave Rs. 2 lacs to plaintiff.

It is further denied that he did not repay Rs.
1.20 lacs to plaintiff.
It is denied that plaintiff had not taken any money from him for the marriage of his nephew.
It is further denied that he had taken Rs. 1.20 lacs from plaintiff for the purposes of the business needs of my son.
It is stated that plaintiff's family was asking for dowry since the inception of marriage.
Defendant no. 1 evidence was closed on 28.01.2020.

11. Thereafter, Defendant no. 2 examined himself as DW2 who tendered his affidavit of evidence as Ex. DW-2 and relied upon documents already exhibited as Ex. DW1/1 and Ex. DW1/B. DW2 was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff on 08.03.2022.
DW2 in his cross-examination has stated that due to loss of Rs. 4 to 5 Lakhs in his business, he had to close the business.
It is denied that he had taken a loan of Rs.1,20,000/- from plaintiff because he had suffered business loss and in need of money.

It is admitted that the cheques were taken prior to the registration of FIR but amount of Rs.1,20,000/- is repayment of part payment of Rs.2,00,000/- which was taken by the plaintiff from him and his family.

It is stated Page no. 6 of 14 (Kanika Agarwal) CJ01/(South) Saket Court/New Delhi MOHAN KUMAR SANGWAN Vs. UPENDRA SINGH AND ANR.

15. The file has been carefully and minutely perused and my issue-wise findings with reasons thereof are as under: -
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to relief of recovery of amount of Rs. 1,20,000/- from the defendants as prayed?
OPP AND Whether the plaintiff is entitled to any interest thereupon?
If yes, at what rate and for which period?
OPP 16.
Both the issued are taken up together as they involve common discussion of law and facts.
The onus to prove both these issues is upon the plaintiff.

Scrutiny of record shows that the defendants has admitted the version of the plaintiff to the extent that the plaintiff had issued two cheques one for an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- and other for Rs. 20,000/- in the name of the defendant no. 1 and 2 respectively.
Hence, the factum of issuance of cheques in favour of defendant no. 1 and 2 is not denied.
What is disputed by the defendants is that the cheques were issued towards loan taken by Page no. 9 of 14 (Kanika Agarwal) CJ01/(South) Saket Court/New Delhi MOHAN KUMAR SANGWAN Vs.

sentences.text: Defendant in his written statement had claimed that the plaintiff has sought a loan of Rs. 2,00,000/- from him in the year 2013 for the wedding of his niece and same was partly returned by the plaintiff by way of two cheques of Rs 1,00,000/- and Rs. 20,000/- each.
In order to corroborate his version, the defendant examined four witnesses including himself.
Now when one see the testimony of DW1/ defendant, it is to be seen that defendant has placed reliance upon interalia Ex. DW1/B and Mark DW1/C (colly) in support of his case.
Ex. DW1/B is the certified copy of charge sheet and Mark DW1/C (colly) is the copy of FIR registered against the plaintiff.
Perusal of these documents shows that defendants have initiated criminal proceedings against the plaintiff under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC.
Thus, the relationship of parties are already filled with bitterness and hostility.

DW1/Defendant during cross-examination was confronted with his statement under Section 161 CrPC Ex. DW1/P2 (colly) made before police official in FIR no. 264/16 wherein the defendant stated that he had advanced Page no. 10 of 14 (Kanika Agarwal) CJ 01/(South) Saket Court/New Delhi MOHAN KUMAR SANGWAN Vs. UPENDRA SINGH AND ANR.
a loan of Rs. 3,00,000/- in the year 2015 to the plaintiff.

sentences.text:
Thus, there appears to be contradiction in the version of defendant between what is stated in his written statement and statement under Section 161 CrPC.
17.
Coming to testimony of DW2, he has admitted in his cross-examination that he had stated a new business in the year 2014 and same had suffered losses.
This statement of DW2 corroborates the version of the plaintiff to the extent that defendant had approached plaintiff for the purpose of his son's business.

Further, DW3 in his cross-examination has stated that a loan of Rs. 2,00,000/- was given to the plaintiff by defendant no. 1 after arranging part amount from others, however, such averments were not mentioned in the written statement.
Further, names of person from whom the amount was borrowed is not disclosed and neither were they examined.

18. As far as version of DW3 is concerned, she has stated in her testimony that a loan of Rs.
2,00,000/- was advanced to plaintiff after he had mercilessly beaten her.
It is incomprehensible that a father would advance a loan to his son-in-law despite his daughter being beaten and ill-treated by her husband.
19. Upon appreciation of evidence lead by both the sides, it is clear that the defendant's version suffers from several contradictions.

On one hand the defendant no.1 claims in his written Page no. 11 of 14 (Kanika Agarwal) CJ01/(South) Saket Court/New Delhi MOHAN KUMAR SANGWAN Vs.
UPENDRA SINGH AND ANR.
statement that he had advanced a loan of Rs 2,00,000/- in the year 2013, however in his statement under Section 161 CrPC, he has stated that loan of Rs 3,00,000/- was given in the year 2015.

sentences.text: Further, even DW3 in her statement under Section 161 CrPC Ex. DW3/P1 has stated that a loan of Rs. 3,00,000/- was advanced to the plaintiff.

Although in few circumstances, such contradictions with regard to difference in date and amount of loan may be of little relevance, however considering the fact that there is absolutely no documentary evidence and independent witness to corroborate the plea of defendants that they had advanced a loan of Rs. 2,00,000/- to the plaintiff, court finds it difficult to believe the version of the defendants in light of the contradictions.

Further, interestingly,

A necessary corollary being that plaintiff has succeeded in establishing their case on scale of preponderance of probabilities.

Now, as far as liability of defendant no. 1 and 2 is concerned, plaintiff has claimed a recovery of Rs.
1,00,000/- from defendant no. 1 and recovery of Rs. 20,000/- from defendant no. 1 and 2 on ground that a sum of Rs. 20,000/- was Page no. 12 of 14 (Kanika Agarwal) CJ01/(South) Saket Court/New Delhi MOHAN KUMAR SANGWAN Vs. UPENDRA SINGH AND ANR.
credited in the account of defendant no. 2.

sentences.text: It is an admitted fact that a cheque of Rs. 1,00,000/- was encashed in favour of defendant no. 1 and Rs. 20,000/- was encashed in favour of defendant no. 2.

Taking into account that it is the defendant no. 1 who had sought a loan of Rs. 20,000/- in the year 2014 and Rs. 1,00,000/- in the year 2015 for the business of defendant no. 2 and that amount of Rs.
1,00,000/- was credited into the account of defendant no. 1 and Rs. 20,000/- was credited into the account of defendant no. 2, therefore, defendant no. 1 is liable to pay Rs. 1,00,000/- to plaintiff whereas defendant no. 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay Rs. 20,000/- to the plaintiff.
Further, court deems fit to award interest @ 6% from the filing of suit i.e. 19.08.2017 till realization.
Hence, these issues are decided against the defendants and in favour of the plaintiff.
Relief.

21. In light of the aforesaid discussion, the suit of the plaintiff is decreed to the effect that defendant no. 1 is liable to pay Rs. 1,00,000/- to the plaintiff whereas defendant no. 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay Rs. 20,000/- to the plaintiff along with interest @ 6% from the filing of suit i.e. 19.08.2017 till real- ization.
22. No order as to cost.

Although in few circumstances, such contradictions with regard to difference in date and amount of loan may be of little relevance, however considering the fact that there is absolutely no documentary evidence and independent witness to corroborate the plea of defendants that they had advanced a loan of Rs. 2,00,000/- to the plaintiff, court finds it difficult to believe the version of the defendants in light of the contradictions.
Further, interestingly,
Mohan Kumar Sangwan vs Upendra Singh And Ans on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51261179/
6 Ld. counsel for defendants during cross-examination of PW1/ plaintiff has given a suggestion that defendants have already paid the amount of Rs. 1,20,000/-, thus indirectly admitting the factum of loan.
20 . Thus, in light of aforesaid discussion and observations, the court is of the opinion that the defendants have failed to corroborate and establish their defence.
A necessary corollary being that plaintiff has succeeded in establishing their case on scale of preponderance of probabilities.
Now, as far as liability of defendant no. 1 and 2 is concerned, plaintiff has claimed a recovery of Rs.
1,00,000/- from defendant no. 1 and recovery of Rs. 20,000/- from defendant no. 1 and 2 on ground that a sum of Rs. 20,000/- was Page no. 12 of 14 (Kanika Agarwal) CJ01/(South) Saket Court/New Delhi MOHAN KUMAR SANGWAN Vs. UPENDRA SINGH AND ANR.
credited in the account of defendant no. 2.
It is an admitted fact that a cheque of Rs. 1,00,000/- was encashed in favour of defendant no. 1 and Rs. 20,000/- was encashed in favour of defendant no. 2.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Taking into account that it is the defendant no. 1 who had sought a loan of Rs. 20,000/- in the year 2014 and Rs. 1,00,000/- in the year 2015 for the business of defendant no. 2 and that amount of Rs.
1,00,000/- was credited into the account of defendant no. 1 and Rs. 20,000/- was credited into the account of defendant no. 2, therefore, defendant no. 1 is liable to pay Rs. 1,00,000/- to plaintiff whereas defendant no. 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay Rs. 20,000/- to the plaintiff.
Further, court deems fit to award interest @ 6% from the filing of suit i.e. 19.08.2017 till realization.
Hence, these issues are decided against the defendants and in favour of the plaintiff.
Relief.
21. In light of the aforesaid discussion, the suit of the plaintiff is decreed to the effect that defendant no. 1 is liable to pay Rs. 1,00,000/- to the plaintiff whereas defendant no. 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay Rs. 20,000/- to the plaintiff along with interest @ 6% from the filing of suit i.e. 19.08.2017 till real- ization.
22. No order as to cost.
